mainTopic: Explaining the משנה's list of who may join a זימון, defining an עם הארץ, and who can complete a group of three or ten
overview: This amud keeps going line by line through the משנה about who may be counted for a זימון. It first finishes אביי's point that a לוי who takes מעשר ראשון from the grain pile still owes תרומה גדולה, because piled grain already counts as 'דגן'. For each case in the משנה, the גמרא asks 'isn't this obvious?' and finds the hidden lesson: unpaid חומש does not hold back a redemption, a שמש counts as part of the meal, rabbinic טבל still disqualifies, and a גר who had מילה but no טבילה is still a נכרי. It explains why a כותי may join even though an עם הארץ may not. This leads to a ברייתא listing many definitions of an עם הארץ, the ruling like אחרים, and the story of רמי בר חמא and רב מנשיא. The גמרא then discusses fillers for a group of ten: a baby in a cradle as a סניף, nine men and one עבד, and רבי אליעזר freeing his slave for a מצוה דרבים. It praises being among the first ten in shul and corrects the surprising sayings about 'nine and an ark' and 'two and שבת'. Finally, רבי יוחנן counts a קטן פורח, and the גמרא begins to examine a puzzling clause in a supporting ברייתא, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי's verse: the לוי must give from all his gifts
steps.stepSummary: אביי completes his answer to רב פפא by quoting a פסוק showing that a לוי who took his מעשר ראשון from the grain pile, before the כהן took תרומה גדולה, must still separate תרומה גדולה from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "From all your tithes you shall set apart [the Lord's portion]."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of אביי's answer from the previous lines. He quotes a פסוק to prove that the לוי must give תרומה גדולה even though he took his tithe early, from the pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ריש לקיש had ruled that a לוי who takes מעשר ראשון early, while the grain is still on its stalks, is exempt from תרומה גדולה. רב פפא asked why that would not also apply once the grain was in a pile. אביי answers that the פסוק says 'from ALL your tithes,' which obligates the לוי in the pile case.

keyTerms.meaning: your tithes (the gifts given to the Levites)
you shall set apart / separate (as a תרומה)
the main תרומה, given to the כהן first
the first tithe, given to the לוי

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the finish of אביי's answer on the previous amud, so read it as part of that earlier discussion.

phrases.english: "From all your tithes you shall set apart."
phrases.notes: This פסוק is the proof: the לוי has to separate תרומה גדולה from all his gifts, even one he took early from the pile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer to רב פפא earlier.
steps.raayaObject: That a לוי who took מעשר ראשון from the pile, before תרומה גדולה was separated, must still give תרומה גדולה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Early מעשר ראשון taken from the pile still owes תרומה גדולה.

steps.title: Why treat the pile differently from the stalks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: the same פסוק could cover the stalks too, so why apply it only to the pile?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see [that made you include the pile and exclude the stalks]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we use the פסוק to obligate the pile case but still exempt the stalks case. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from all' sound like they include everything. So the גמרא wants to know what reason lets us keep ריש לקיש's exemption for grain on its stalks, while obligating grain in the pile.

keyTerms.meaning: and what did you see? (what is your reason for this distinction?)
a pile of threshed grain
stalks / ears of grain

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He's asking: why say 'from all' covers the pile and not the grain still on the stalks?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the פסוק from step 1 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's choice to apply 'מכל' to the pile but not to the stalks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'from all' includes everything, the stalks case should be included as well.

steps.title: Piled grain has become 'grain'; stalks have not
steps.stepSummary: Answer: once grain is threshed and piled, it is called דגן, so the כהן's right to תרומה has already begun. Grain still on the stalk is not yet דגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one has become grain, and that one has not become grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference. Piled grain already counts as 'grain' (דגן), but grain still on the stalk does not yet count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about תרומה says 'ראשית דגנך' (the first of your grain). Once the grain is in a pile, it is דגן, so the כהן's claim has already started, and the לוי cannot avoid it by taking his tithe first. While the grain is on the stalk, the obligation has not started yet, so the exemption still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: it has become דגן (fully processed grain)
grain, the word used in the פסוק about תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: A לוי who takes his tithe early is exempt from תרומה גדולה only if he took it while the grain was still on the stalks. Once the grain is piled, it is 'דגן' and the obligation applies.

phrases.english: This one has become grain, and that one has not become grain.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the pile; 'that one' is the grain still on the stalks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the stage of processing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'from all' should include both the stalks and the pile.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only grain that has become דגן (the pile) is obligated. Grain on the stalks is not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Piled grain is דגן and obligated in תרומה גדולה. Grain on the stalk is not yet.

steps.title: Redeemed second tithe and consecrated food: isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, that one who ate מעשר שני or הקדש that was redeemed may join the זימון, and asks why this needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] Second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed [may be counted]. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and complains that it seems obvious. Once something is redeemed, it is plain regular food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeemed מעשר שני or הקדש loses its holiness and becomes ordinary food, so eating it is a normal meal. The גמרא asks what new point the משנה is teaching by saying this.

keyTerms.meaning: the second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
property consecrated to the בית המקדש
that were redeemed (their holiness moved onto money)
it is obvious! (why say it?)

phrases.english: Second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed:
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case listed in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to mention redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redeemed food is plainly ordinary food, so the ruling teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The case is where the extra fifth was not paid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about someone who paid the main value (קרן) but not the added חומש. It teaches that the missing חומש does not hold back the redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he paid the principal but did not pay the fifth. And this teaches us that the fifth does not hold back [the redemption].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. The person paid the main price but not the extra fifth, and the משנה tells us the food still counts as redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who redeems his own מעשר שני or הקדש must add a fifth (חומש) on top of the value. You might think that without the חומש the redemption is incomplete. The משנה teaches that paying the קרן alone completes the redemption, so the food is ordinary and the eater joins the זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here? (the גמרא narrows the case)
principal, the main value of the item
the added fifth paid when redeeming one's own item
does not hold back / does not invalidate
it teaches us (the new point)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule about redemption: the חומש is still owed, but it is not required for the redemption to take effect.
steps.confusionAlert: The חומש is still owed. The point is only that not paying it yet does not stop the redemption from working.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he gave the principal,
but did not give the fifth.
And this teaches us
that the fifth does not hold back [the redemption].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 4 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the חומש, the food might still be holy and not count as a regular meal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Paying the קרן alone completes the redemption, because the חומש does not hold it back.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אין חומש מעכב: the redemption works even before the fifth is paid.

steps.title: The waiter who ate an olive's worth: isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a שמש who ate a כזית may join the זימון, and asks why this needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] The waiter who ate an olive's worth [may be counted]. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and again asks why it needed saying. Anyone who ate a כזית normally joins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a כזית is the usual minimum for joining a זימון. So the גמרא asks what is special about a waiter that the משנה had to mention him.

keyTerms.meaning: a waiter / attendant who serves the diners
an olive's volume, the minimum amount of eating

phrases.english: The waiter who ate an olive's worth:
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case listed in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to mention the שמש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anyone who ate a כזית joins, so naming the waiter seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A waiter does count as part of the meal
steps.stepSummary: You might have thought that a waiter, who eats while standing and serving, has not truly joined the meal. The משנה teaches that he has.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: a waiter has not set himself [as part of the meal]. So it teaches us [that he has].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point. Even though the waiter is busy serving and eats on the go, he still counts as a real participant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זימון requires people who have 'set' themselves (קבע) as part of the meal. A waiter who eats in snatches might seem not to qualify. The משנה rules that his eating still counts as joining the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
set himself / established himself as part of the meal

phrases.english: You might have said:
a waiter has not established [himself in the meal],
so it teaches us [that he has].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: removing a reasonable mistaken assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A waiter eats without settling into the meal, so he should not join the זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: A waiter who ate a כזית does count as having joined the meal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שמש who ate a כזית joins the זימון.

steps.title: Why can a כותי join if an עם הארץ cannot?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that a כותי may join a זימון. At best he is like an עם הארץ, and a ברייתא says an עם הארץ may not be counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] And a כותי may be counted for a זימון. Why? Let him be no better than an עם הארץ! And a ברייתא teaches: we do not count an עם הארץ for a זימון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and attacks it using a ברייתא. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if we treat the כותי as Jewish, he is at most like an עם הארץ, someone careless about purity and tithes. A ברייתא says an עם הארץ is not counted for a זימון. So how can the משנה count a כותי?

keyTerms.meaning: a Samaritan, whose Jewish status was questioned
we count him for a זימון
let him be no more than (at most he is)
an unlearned Jew who is not careful about purity and tithes

phrases.english: And a Kuti, we count him for a zimmun:

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי? לֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא עַם הָאָרֶץ!
phrases.english: Why? Let him be no more than an am ha'aretz!

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עַל עַם הָאָרֶץ!
phrases.english: And it was taught: we do not count an am ha'aretz for a zimmun!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה, this time with a real contradiction from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a כותי may be counted for a זימון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'לא יהא אלא' reasoning: at most a כותי has the status of an עם הארץ, and a ברייתא excludes an עם הארץ, so the כותי should be excluded too.

steps.title: אביי: The כותי Is a Trustworthy חבר
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה is talking about a כותי who is a חבר, so he is not an עם הארץ at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the משנה is talking about a כותי who is a חבר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the challenge from Step 8. אביי says the כותי in the משנה is a careful, trustworthy person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that a כותי is at best like an עם הארץ, who may not be counted. אביי answers by narrowing the case: the משנה means a כותי who is a חבר, someone careful about the מצוות. Such a person is clearly not an עם הארץ, so he may be counted.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan, from a group whose Jewish status and observance were in question
A person known to be careful about tithes and purity
An unlearned or less careful person, defined differently by different opinions

phrases.english: Abaye said:
[The Mishnah speaks] of a Kuti who is a chaver.
phrases.notes: He is careful about the מצוות, so he is not an עם הארץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow any כותי, even one who is like an עם הארץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only allows a כותי who is a חבר.

steps.title: רבא: The חכמים' Definition of an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even a כותי who is an עם הארץ may join, because the rule excluding an עם הארץ follows the חכמים. They define an עם הארץ as someone who does not tithe properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: even if the כותי is an עם הארץ, he can still be counted. The ברייתא that excludes an עם הארץ uses the definition of the חכמים, who argue with רבי מאיר. A ברייתא says: Who is an עם הארץ? רבי מאיר says it is anyone who does not eat his ordinary food in purity. The חכמים say it is anyone who does not tithe his produce properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the challenge. רבא says the word עם הארץ has different definitions, and the excluded עם הארץ is the one defined by the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not need the כותי to be a חבר. He explains that the ruling against counting an עם הארץ uses the חכמים' definition, which is someone who does not tithe. Under רבי מאיר's stricter definition, even a person who tithes could be an עם הארץ, but that is not the definition used here.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say; it introduces an answer that works even in the harder case
Eating ordinary, non-holy food while keeping the purity laws
Tithes his produce
They disagree

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even if you say [it refers to] a Kuti who is an am ha'aretz,
here [in the baraita] it is about an am ha'aretz as defined by the Rabbis
who disagree with Rabbi Meir, that we are dealing with,
as it was taught: Who is an am ha'aretz?
Anyone who does not eat his ordinary food in purity,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
Anyone who does not tithe his produce properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּכוּתִי עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same challenge that אביי answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the term in the challenging source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any עם הארץ, by any definition, is excluded, and a כותי falls into that group.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an עם הארץ by the חכמים' definition, one who does not tithe, is excluded.

steps.title: Why כותים Pass the חכמים' Test
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that כותים tithe properly, because they are very careful about מצוות written in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: These כותים do tithe properly, because they are very careful about what is written in the Torah. As the Master said: any מצוה the כותים took on, they are more exacting in it than Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's answer by showing why a כותי does not fit the חכמים' definition of an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithing is written in the Torah, and כותים keep written Torah מצוות very carefully. So by the חכמים' test of not tithing, a כותי is not an עם הארץ. A teaching from מר supports this: כותים are even more exacting than Jews in the מצוות they accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: They certainly tithe
They are very careful
They took hold of it; they accepted the מצוה upon themselves
They are exacting and precise

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers about the כותי: אביי says he is a חבר. רבא says the excluded עם הארץ is one who does not tithe, and כותים tithe carefully.

phrases.english: And these Kutim
do tithe properly, as is fitting,
for in what is written in the Torah
they are very careful.
As the Master said:
Any מצוה that the Kutim took upon themselves
they are very exacting in it, more than Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by applying the חכמים' definition to כותים.
steps.raayaObject: That a כותי is not an עם הארץ under the חכמים' definition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of מר that כותים are very exacting in the מצוות they accepted.

steps.title: A ברייתא Lists Many Definitions of עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives more opinions on who is an עם הארץ: someone who does not say קריאת שמע, does not wear תפילין, has no ציצית, has no מזוזה, does not raise his children to learn Torah, or learned without serving תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Who is an עם הארץ? Anyone who does not say קריאת שמע at night and in the morning; these are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע says: anyone who does not put on תפילין. בן עזאי says: anyone who has no ציצית on his garment. רבי נתן says: anyone who has no מזוזה on his doorway. רבי נתן בר יוסף says: anyone who has children and does not raise them to learn Torah. אחרים say: even if he learned Torah and משנה but did not serve תלמידי חכמים, he is an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was just discussing definitions of עם הארץ, it brings a related ברייתא with even more definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion points to a different basic מצוה whose neglect makes someone an עם הארץ. The last opinion, אחרים, is the most demanding. Learning on your own is not enough. You must also serve תלמידי חכמים to understand what you learned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others'; an unnamed תנא, often identified as רבי מאיר
He learned Torah (the written text) and משנה
He served Torah scholars and learned the reasons from them

steps.confusionAlert: Different meanings of עם הארץ apply in different contexts. In this ברייתא it means someone lacking in basic מצוות or in learning. That is not the same as the tithing definition used for the כותי above.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Who is an am ha'aretz?
Anyone who does not recite Shema
evening and morning; these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: anyone who does not put on tefillin.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ צִיצִית בְּבִגְדוֹ.
phrases.english: Ben Azzai says: anyone who has no tzitzis on his garment.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מְזוּזָה עַל פִּתְחוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: anyone who has no mezuzah on his doorway.
Rabbi Natan bar Yosef says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים וְאֵינוֹ מְגַדְּלָם לְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: Anyone who has sons and does not raise them to Torah study.
Others say: even if he learned Scripture and Mishnah

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שִׁמֵּשׁ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הֲרֵי זֶה עַם הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: but did not serve Torah scholars, he is an am ha'aretz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the topic of defining עם הארץ, which came up in רבא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are many opinions on who is an עם הארץ. The strictest, אחרים, includes even a learned person who did not serve תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: רב הונא Rules Like אחרים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the הלכה follows אחרים: one who learned but did not serve תלמידי חכמים is an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the הלכה follows אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the ברייתא's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of all the opinions, רב הונא picks the strictest one. This ruling sets up the story that comes next, where someone applies this rule in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha follows...

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the background for the story of רמי בר חמא. He relied on it to exclude רב מנשיא בר תחליפא from a זימון.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: The halacha is in accordance with Others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the opinions listed in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who learned but did not serve תלמידי חכמים is considered an עם הארץ.

steps.title: The Story of רמי בר חמא and רב מנשיא
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא did not count רב מנשיא בר תחליפא, a learned man, for a זימון. When רמי בר חמא died, רבא said he died because of this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא did not include רב מנשיא בר תחליפא in a זימון, even though רב מנשיא learned ספרא, ספרי, and הלכות. When רמי בר חמא died, רבא said: רמי בר חמא died only because he did not include רב מנשיא בר תחליפא in a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that seems to connect to the ruling of אחרים. It sets up a question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא apparently treated רב מנשיא as an עם הארץ, the type who learned but did not serve scholars. רבא saw רמי בר חמא's death as a punishment for this. That means excluding רב מנשיא was a serious mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Included him in a זימון
Collections of halachic teachings on ויקרא, and on במדבר and דברים
His soul came to rest; he died

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לָא אַזְמֵין עֲלֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama did not include in a zimmun
Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa,
who had learned Sifra, Sifrei, and halachos.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, אָמַר רָבָא:
phrases.english: When Rami bar Chama died, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama died only

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּלָא אַזְמֵין אַרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא.
phrases.english: because he did not include Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa in a zimmun.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לָא אַזְמֵין עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing the rule of אחרים in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Excluding a true scholar from a זימון is a grave wrong.

steps.title: But אחרים Say Such a Person Is an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to אחרים, someone who learned but did not serve scholars is an עם הארץ. So why was רמי בר חמא punished?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: אחרים say that even if he learned Torah and משנה but did not serve תלמידי חכמים, he is an עם הארץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's statement. רמי בר חמא seems to have acted correctly according to the halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Halacha follows אחרים, and by that rule one who only learned is an עם הארץ. If רב מנשיא only learned ספרא and ספרי, then רמי בר חמא was right to exclude him. Why, then, was he punished?

phrases.english: But it was taught: Others say,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ קָרָא וְשָׁנָה וְלֹא שִׁמֵּשׁ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
phrases.english: even if he learned Scripture and Mishnah but did not serve Torah scholars,
he is an am ha'aretz?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's statement in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רמי בר חמא was punished for not including רב מנשיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the accepted ruling of אחרים, רב מנשיא counts as an עם הארץ, so excluding him was correct.

steps.title: רב מנשיא Actually Served the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב מנשיא did serve the Sages. רמי בר חמא simply did not check carefully into his background.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר תחליפא is different, because he served the חכמים. It was רמי בר חמא who did not investigate him carefully.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב מנשיא was not an עם הארץ even by the definition of אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of אחרים is not being questioned. The facts were different: רב מנשיא had served scholars. רמי בר חמא's mistake was that he did not check before judging him as an עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Serves the Rabbis
He did not check carefully after him

phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa is different,
because he served the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: וְרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא הוּא דְּלָא דָּק אַבָּתְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and it was Rami bar Chama who did not look carefully into him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15 by clarifying the facts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מנשיא only learned and never served scholars.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did serve scholars. רמי בר חמא failed to check.

steps.title: Another Version: Hearing From the Sages Makes One a Scholar
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the answer: anyone who hears teachings from the Sages and reviews them is considered a young scholar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: one who heard teachings from the mouths of the Rabbis and reviewed them is like a young Torah scholar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an alternative version of the answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version explains what counts as serving תלמידי חכמים. Hearing teachings directly from the Sages and reviewing them is enough to make one a צורבא מרבנן. רב מנשיא was like this, so he was not an עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version
Halachic teachings
Reviews and studies
A young Torah scholar

steps.whatToRemember: Excluding a real scholar from a זימון is serious. Anyone who learned teachings directly from the Sages counts as a scholar, not an עם הארץ.

phrases.english: Another version:
One who heard teachings from the mouths of the Rabbis
and studies them is considered like a young Torah scholar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative version of the answer given in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining what counts as serving scholars
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only formal, long-term service of scholars removes the label עם הארץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hearing and reviewing teachings from the Sages is enough to be a צורבא מרבנן.

steps.title: Isn't It Obvious That Eating טבל Doesn't Count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that one who ate טבל may not join a זימון, and asks why this is not obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who ate טבל or מעשר and so on. About טבל, isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks why it needed to teach the case of טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating טבל is forbidden. Clearly someone who ate forbidden food cannot make a זימון on it, so why did the משנה need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required tithes have not yet been taken; it is forbidden to eat
It is obvious

phrases.english: [The Mishnah:] If he ate tevel or ma'aser etc.
Tevel, that is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל טֶבֶל וּמַעֲשֵׂר וְכוּ׳: טֶבֶל פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to going through the משנה's cases, like Steps 4 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one who ate טבל is not counted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating טבל is plainly forbidden, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: טבל Only מדרבנן: An Unperforated Pot
steps.stepSummary: The משנה refers to produce that is טבל only מדרבנן, such as produce grown in an unperforated pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed for produce that is טבל by rabbinic law. What is the case? Produce grown in a pot with no hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is teaching something new: even rabbinic טבל prevents a person from being counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce grown in a pot without a hole is not connected to the ground. Because of this, the Torah does not require it to be tithed. The חכמים still require tithes, and the משנה teaches that eating such produce also keeps a person out of the זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for... (introduces the non-obvious case)
Untithed by rabbinic law
What is the case?
A flowerpot without a hole

steps.confusionAlert: Produce in a pot without a hole is still produce. The Torah tithing obligation simply does not apply to it, because it did not grow from the ground. The obligation to tithe it comes only from the חכמים.

phrases.english: It is only needed for tevel that is untithed by rabbinic law.
What is the case? In an unperforated flowerpot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since rabbinic טבל is permitted by the Torah, eating it might still allow a זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even rabbinic טבל prevents the eater from joining a זימון.

steps.title: Why the משנה needs to mention מעשר ראשון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of one who ate מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken, and asks why this is not obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one who ate מעשר ראשון (whose תרומה was not taken) can't join a זימון. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and asks why it even needs to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תרומה was never taken from the מעשר ראשון, the food is still forbidden. Eating forbidden food obviously can't count toward a זימון. So why does the משנה bother to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, the tenth of produce given to a לוי
It is obvious, used to challenge why something needed to be taught
Etc.: the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: First tithe, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: first tithe from which its תרומה was not taken.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same 'פשיטא' pattern used for טבל in step 18, now applied to the next case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of מעשר ראשון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food still forbidden by its untaken תרומה obviously cannot count for a זימון, so the case seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The case where the Levite took his share from the pile
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means a case where the לוי took his מעשר from the grain pile before the כהן took תרומה. We might have thought this was exempt, like רב פפא suggested, but the משנה teaches like אביי's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where the לוי went first, taking his share once the grain was in a pile. You might have said like רב פפא said to אביי (that it is exempt from תרומה גדולה). The משנה teaches us like אביי answered him (that it is not exempt).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה refers to a tricky case: the לוי took his מעשר ראשון after the grain was already piled, before the כהן got his תרומה גדולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the sugya we learned that if the לוי takes his share while the grain is still on the stalks, he does not have to give תרומה גדולה from it. רב פפא asked: why not say the same when it is already in a pile? אביי answered that once grain is piled it is already obligated in תרומה, so the לוי's share still owes תרומה גדולה. The משנה follows אביי, so eating it is eating forbidden food.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for: introduces a narrower, less obvious case
He went first: the לוי took his share before the כהן
A pile of grain that has already been threshed and smoothed
You might have said: introduces the mistaken assumption
It teaches us: introduces the real lesson
As he answered him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Stalks: the לוי's share is exempt from תרומה גדולה. Pile: it is NOT exempt. Our משנה is about the pile.

phrases.english: It is only needed where he (the Levite) went first, in the pile.
phrases.notes: The grain had already been gathered into a pile before the לוי took his share.

phrases.english: You might have said
as Rav Pappa said to Abaye
phrases.notes: רב פפא suggested the pile case should also be exempt.

phrases.english: it teaches us as he (Abaye) answered him.
phrases.notes: אביי's answer was that once the grain is piled, it already has to have תרומה taken from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 20 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (לא צריכא) to a non-obvious scenario
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Like רב פפא: מעשר ראשון taken from the pile should be exempt from תרומה גדולה, just like when taken from the stalks.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like אביי: in the pile it is still obligated, so it remains forbidden and cannot count for a זימון.

steps.title: Why the משנה needs to mention מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about מעשר שני and הקדש that were not redeemed, and asks why this is not obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one who ate מעשר שני (or הקדש that was not redeemed) can't join a זימון. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and again asks why it needs to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני outside ירושלים and unredeemed הקדש are clearly forbidden to eat. So it seems obvious that eating them cannot count toward a זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Etc.: the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Second tithe, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: second tithe and consecrated food that were not redeemed.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same פשיטא pattern, applied to the next item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of unredeemed מעשר שני and הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unredeemed holy food is plainly forbidden, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Second tithe redeemed with an unminted coin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means items that were 'redeemed' but not in the proper way. For מעשר שני, it was redeemed with a blank coin, but the Torah requires money with a stamped image.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where they were redeemed, but not redeemed properly. מעשר שני: for example, he redeemed it with a blank coin. But the Torah says 'וצרת הכסף בידך': money that has an image on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a redemption that happened but was invalid. It starts with the מעשר שני example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the person did a redemption, we might think the food became permitted. But the word 'וצרת' hints at 'צורה', a stamped image. So a blank coin (אסימון) does not work, and the מעשר שני stays holy and forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their law: in the proper way
A blank coin or metal disc with no stamped image
The Merciful One: the Torah
A stamped image or form on a coin

phrases.english: It is only needed where they were redeemed
but were not redeemed properly.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי — כְּגוֹן שֶׁפְּדָאוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי אֲסִימוֹן,
phrases.english: Second tithe: for example, he redeemed it with an unminted coin,
and the Torah said: 'And bind up the money in your hand'
money that has an image on it.
phrases.notes: The word וצרת is being read as if it comes from צורה, an image.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ וְלֹא נִפְדּוּ כְּהִלְכָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a flawed redemption, supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he did some kind of redemption, the מעשר שני should be permitted and count for a זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: A blank coin is not valid money for redemption, so the food is still forbidden.

steps.title: Consecrated property redeemed with land
steps.stepSummary: The second example of a flawed redemption: הקדש exchanged for land instead of money. The Torah requires money.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדש: where he redeemed it with land and not with money. But the Torah says 'ונתן הכסף וקם לו': he gives money and it becomes his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer with the הקדש example of a redemption that does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person tried to redeem the הקדש by giving land in exchange. The פסוק says 'he will give the money', so הקדש must be redeemed with money. Since land is not money, the food stays holy and forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
He redeemed it, taking away its holiness
Land

phrases.english: Consecrated property: where he redeemed it with land,
and did not redeem it with money,
and the Torah said: 'He will give the money and it will be his.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 23's answer, applying the same idea to הקדש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a flawed redemption, supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exchanging the הקדש for land should remove its holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: הקדש can only be redeemed with money, so it stays forbidden.

steps.title: Why the משנה needs to mention a waiter who ate less than a כזית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a שמש who ate less than a כזית and asks why this is not obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a waiter who ate less than a כזית can't join a זימון. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and asks why it needs to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זימון requires eating at least a כזית. Someone who ate less obviously does not qualify, so the line seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A waiter who serves the meal
Less than an olive's volume, the minimum amount for a זימון

phrases.english: And the waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk:
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same פשיטא pattern for the next item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of a שמש who ate less than a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Less than the minimum amount clearly does not count.

steps.title: Listed only to match the first clause
steps.stepSummary: Since the first half of the משנה mentioned a כזית, the second half mentions less than a כזית to keep the wording parallel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the first part of the משנה taught 'a כזית', the last part taught 'less than a כזית'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the case really is obvious. The משנה included it only for matching style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is different from the earlier ones. The גמרא does not find a hidden case here. It explains that the משנה mentioned a כזית in the first half, so it phrased the second half as its opposite for balance.

keyTerms.meaning: Since: because of something else that was said
The first clause of the משנה
The last clause of the משנה

phrases.english: Since the first clause taught 'an olive-bulk',
the last clause taught 'less than an olive-bulk'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by explaining the wording, not by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism (אגב / אַיְּידִי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case in the משנה must teach some new rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: This case is truly obvious. It is listed only to match the רישא.

steps.title: Why the משנה needs to say a נכרי is not included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a נכרי is not counted for a זימון and asks why this is not obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said we don't make a זימון with a נכרי. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last case in this part of the משנה and asks why it is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נכרי is not obligated in ברכת המזון. So of course he can't be counted toward a זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: A gentile
Count him toward a זימון

phrases.english: And a gentile is not included in a זימון:
It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same פשיטא pattern for the next item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling about a נכרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gentile has no obligation in ברכת המזון, so excluding him is obvious.

steps.title: A convert circumcised but not yet immersed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a גר who had ברית מילה but has not yet gone to the מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A convert who was circumcised but did not yet immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'נכרי' here means a convert in the middle of the conversion process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once someone has had a ברית מילה, we might think he already counts as Jewish. The משנה teaches that he is still a נכרי for זימון until he also immerses.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Introduces a specific scenario
A convert
Was circumcised
Immersed in a מקוה

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a convert who was circumcised but did not immerse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 by narrowing 'נכרי' to a partial convert.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A convert who had ברית מילה already counts as a Jew for זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without טבילה he is still a נכרי and is not counted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: no גר until מילה and טבילה
steps.stepSummary: Support from רבי זירא in the name of רבי יוחנן: a person is not a גר until he has both מילה and טבילה. Until he immerses, he is a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי זירא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a person is never a convert until he is circumcised and immerses. As long as he did not immerse, he is a gentile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a rule from רבי יוחנן about how conversion is completed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says conversion needs both steps, מילה and טבילה. So a man who has had only מילה is still fully a גוי. That is why the משנה calls him a נכרי and excludes him from a זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: Never, under any circumstance
And immerses
As long as he has not

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list is explained case by case. Most cases are narrowed to a less obvious version: the pile case for מעשר ראשון, a flawed redemption for מעשר שני and הקדש, and a half-converted גר for the נכרי. The שמש case is included only to match the wording of the first half.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוחנן's rule that a גר needs both מילה and טבילה is a basic rule in the הלכות of conversion.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One is never a convert
until he is circumcised and immerses,
and as long as he did not immerse, he is a gentile.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that supports the answer in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That a convert who was circumcised but did not immerse is still considered a נכרי
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא in the name of רבי יוחנן: one is not a גר until both מילה and טבילה

steps.title: A baby in a cradle can be counted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are not counted for a זימון. It then brings רבי יוסי, who says a baby lying in a cradle is counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women, slaves, and minors are not counted for a זימון. רבי יוסי said: a minor lying in a cradle is counted for a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the משנה and then a surprising statement from רבי יוסי. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says קטנים are not counted. רבי יוסי seems to go further in the opposite direction, since he counts even a tiny baby who cannot do anything. That obvious tension is what the גמרא attacks in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We include them in a זימון (the group invitation to bensch)
A minor, a child under בר מצוה
Lying in a cradle, meaning a tiny baby
Non-Jewish slaves owned by a Jew, who keep only some מצוות

phrases.english: Women, slaves, and minors
are not counted for a zimmun.
Rabbi Yosei said:
A minor lying in a cradle
is counted for a zimmun.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה after the discussion of the נכרי and the גר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a baby lying in a cradle is counted for a זימון.

steps.title: But the משנה says minors are not counted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי can count a baby when the משנה says קטנים are not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: women, slaves, and minors are not counted for a זימון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי from the plain words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even an older child is not counted, a baby in a cradle certainly should not be counted. רבי יוסי seems to contradict the משנה directly.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? It opens a challenge from a source.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
Women, slaves, and minors
are not counted for a zimmun!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוסי's statement from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling that a baby in a cradle is counted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says קטנים are not counted, so a baby certainly is not.

steps.title: A baby can be a filler for ten
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי follows רבי יהושע בן לוי. A baby does not count toward a basic זימון, but he can be a סניף (filler) to complete ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds like רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: even though they said a baby in a cradle is not counted for a זימון, he can still be made a filler to complete ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי does not argue with the משנה. He only means the baby can help complete a group of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels. The משנה is talking about the basic group of three, and there a קטן never counts. רבי יוסי is talking about completing ten (the level where שם ה׳ is added), and there a baby can be added as a סניף to a group that is already mostly adults.

keyTerms.meaning: An add-on or filler that helps complete a number but does not form the core group
For ten, the level of זימון where שם ה׳ is mentioned
Even though they said

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי makes a baby a full member of the זימון. The baby is only a filler for ten. He still never counts toward the basic three.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of a סניף, someone who cannot form a group on his own but can complete one. The rest of this passage keeps discussing that idea.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.
For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Even though they said
a minor lying in a cradle
is not counted for a zimmun,
one may still make him a filler to complete ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31 by narrowing what רבי יוסי meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the two sources speak about different levels of זימון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי counts a baby as a full member of the זימון, against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A baby does not count toward the basic זימון, but he can be a סניף to complete ten.

steps.title: Nine men and a slave join together
steps.stepSummary: Another ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי: nine free Jewish men plus one עבד combine to make ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: nine and a slave combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from the same רבי יהושע בן לוי on the same topic of completing ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the משנה says an עבד is not counted for a זימון, here an עבד can be the tenth, much like the baby was a filler. This ruling will be challenged in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They join together or combine to make the required number
A slave

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Nine and a slave join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ruling from the same אמורא about completing ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine free men plus one עבד can make ten.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר had to free his slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי from the story of רבי אליעזר, who freed his slave to complete ten. This suggests an unfreed slave does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: There was a story about רבי אליעזר, who came into a shul and did not find ten. He freed his slave and completed the ten with him. So only if he frees him does he count. If he does not free him, he does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling of step 33 using a story from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a slave could already be the tenth, רבי אליעזר would not have needed to free him. Freeing a slave is a big step (normally discouraged), so doing it shows that a slave as he is cannot count.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought as a source for halacha
He freed (his slave)
And he completed (the number) with him

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
There was an incident with Rabbi Eliezer
who entered the synagogue
and did not find ten,
and he freed his slave
and completed the ten with him.
If he freed him, yes,
if he did not free him, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that nine men and an עבד combine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר freed his slave in order to count him. That implies an unfreed slave cannot count.

steps.title: Two were missing: one freed, one counted as a slave
steps.stepSummary: Two people were missing. רבי אליעזר freed one slave, and the second slave counted as the tenth without being freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two were needed. He freed one, and fulfilled the requirement with the other one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story actually fits רבי יהושע בן לוי. There were only eight men, not nine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one slave can join with nine free men. With eight, רבי אליעזר freed one slave to make nine free men, and then the second slave, still a slave, completed ten. The story proves a slave can be the tenth, just not two slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Two were needed
And he fulfilled (the requirement) with one

steps.whatToRemember: A סניף can complete ten but cannot form the core group. A baby in a cradle can be a filler for ten, and nine free men plus one עבד make ten. Only one slave may be the filler, which is why רבי אליעזר freed one of two.

phrases.english: Two were needed,
he freed one
and fulfilled the requirement with the other one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 34 by re-reading the facts of the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the facts of the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one person was missing, so freeing the slave shows an unfreed slave cannot count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two were missing. One slave was freed and the other counted as a slave, which supports רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: How could רבי אליעזר free his slave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story of רבי אליעזר. רב יהודה says that freeing a slave breaks a positive commandment.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do that? Didn't רב יהודה say: anyone who frees his slave breaks a positive commandment, as it says: 'Forever you shall make them serve'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of רבי אליעזר from Step 34, which Step 35 explained. In that story he freed his slave to complete ten, and the גמרא now asks how he was allowed to do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה rules that freeing a עבד כנעני breaks an עשה, based on the פסוק 'לעולם בהם תעבודו'. That makes רבי אליעזר's action look forbidden. So the challenge is against the story itself, not against רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: And how could he do this? (questions whether an action was allowed)
One who frees his slave
Breaks a positive commandment
'Forever you shall make them serve' (ויקרא כה:מו)

phrases.english: And how could he do that?
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי אליעזר freeing his slave

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say:
Anyone who frees his slave breaks a positive commandment,
as it says: 'Forever you shall make them serve'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רבי אליעזר's action in the story (quoted in Step 34, explained in Step 35) was allowed
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's act of freeing his slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה says freeing a slave breaks an עשה, so a great sage should not have done it

steps.title: A מצוה situation is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that freeing a slave for the sake of a מצוה is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the sake of a מצוה it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer: רבי אליעזר freed the slave in order to do a מצוה (completing a מניין), so it was allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on freeing a slave is not absolute. When the freeing is done to make a מצוה possible, the גמרא suggests the ban does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of a מצוה
It is different

phrases.english: For the sake of a מצוה it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the prohibition: a מצוה purpose is an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Freeing a slave is always forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: When it is done for a מצוה, it is allowed

steps.title: But it is a מצוה הבאה בעבירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a מצוה done by breaking a commandment is a מצוה הבאה בעבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is a מצוה that comes through a sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of Step 37: you cannot do a מצוה by first breaking a commandment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of מצוה הבאה בעבירה says a מצוה that is made possible by a sin is flawed. Here, completing the מניין required breaking the עשה of keeping slaves. So 'it's for a מצוה' does not seem to be enough of an excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה that comes about through a sin; it is not counted properly

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question about the slave. It attacks the answer just given (Step 37), showing that 'for a מצוה' alone cannot excuse a sin.

phrases.english: It is a מצוה that comes through a sin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 37
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a מצוה purpose allows freeing the slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מצוה achieved through a sin is invalid, so the מצוה cannot justify the sin

steps.title: A מצוה דרבים is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a מצוה דרבים, a מצוה that helps many people, is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה of the many is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its answer. Freeing the slave is allowed because the מצוה helps the whole community, which needs a מניין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every מצוה justifies freeing a slave, but a מצוה that serves the public does. A מניין lets the whole group say דברים שבקדושה, so the public benefit outweighs the עשה. This closes the challenge to the story of רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה that benefits the public

steps.whatToRemember: Freeing a slave is normally an עבירה, but it is allowed for a מצוה דרבים, like completing a מניין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a public מצוה can carry more weight than a private one, a principle used elsewhere in הלכה.

phrases.english: A מצוה of the many is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 38 by narrowing the exception to public מצוות
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refines the exception: only a public מצוה overrides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any מצוה purpose is a flawed מצוה הבאה בעבירה
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצוה דרבים is different, so freeing the slave to complete ten is allowed

steps.title: The reward for being among the first ten in shul
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says a person should come early to shul to be among the first ten, because he receives the reward of all who come after.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A person should always get up early to go to shul, so that he will merit to be counted among the first ten. For even if a hundred come after him, he receives the reward of all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי about a group of ten, praising those who form the first מניין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ten are the ones who create the מניין; everyone who comes later just joins it. Because of that, the first ten get special reward. The exact wording 'the reward of all of them' will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Get up early
The first ten
The reward of all of them

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A person should always rise early to the synagogue
so that he will merit and be counted
among the first ten,
for even if a hundred come after him,
he receives the reward of all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: לְעוֹלָם יַשְׁכִּים אָדָם לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי on the theme of ten
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first ten in shul receive great reward because they form the מניין that everyone else joins

steps.title: Does he really take everyone else's reward?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording: the first ten cannot take away the reward of those who come later.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The reward of all of them'? Can that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the wording of Step 40. It sounds as if the latecomers lose their reward to the early person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying he 'receives their reward' suggests the others lose theirs, which makes no sense; they did nothing wrong. This is a challenge to the wording, not to the idea that coming early is good.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (shows something is impossible)

phrases.english: 'The reward of all of them'? Could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of Step 40
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It implies the latecomers lose their own reward, which is unfair and illogical

steps.title: He gets a reward equal to all of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the teaching: he gets a reward equal to everyone else's, without taking theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: they give him a reward equal to all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The early person gets a reward as big as everyone's, while they keep their own reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody loses anything. The first ten get extra reward equal in size to the reward of all the others, because they made it possible for everyone to join.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (fixes the wording)
Equal to all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The first ten in shul get a reward equal to everyone who comes after them. The others do not lose their reward.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
they give him a reward equal to all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: נוֹתְנִין לוֹ שָׂכָר כְּנֶגֶד כּוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 41 by rewording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (אלא אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He takes the others' reward
steps.terutzMaskana: He gets a reward equal to theirs, and they keep their own

steps.title: Nine and an ark join together
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says nine people plus the ארון (the Torah ark) join to make a מניין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Nine and an ark join together.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins about joining for a מניין. רב הונא makes a surprising statement that nine men and the ארון count as ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, this says an object can be counted like a person. That sounds strange, and the next step will challenge it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ark where the ספרי תורה are kept
They join together (to complete a group)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Nine and an ark join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: תִּשְׁעָה וְאָרוֹן מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New statement on the theme of completing ten
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine men and the ארון join to form a מניין

steps.title: Is an ark a person?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects that an ark is not a man and cannot be counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Is an ark a man?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא: only people can be counted in a מניין, not objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מניין needs ten men. An ark, however holy, is not a person. So the literal statement cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: A man, a person

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
Is an ark a man?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: וְאָרוֹן גַּבְרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 43
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that an ark joins the nine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only people count toward ten, and an ark is not a person

steps.title: Nine who look like ten join together
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's statement is restated: nine who appear like ten can join.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא said: Nine who look like ten join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the 'ark' version with a new version of רב הונא's teaching. The ark is dropped completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new rule is about how the group looks: if nine people appear like ten, they may join. The question of what makes nine look like ten is discussed in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Look like ten

steps.confusionAlert: The ark is no longer part of the rule at all. The final version says nothing about an object counting; it is only about nine people who look like ten.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna said:
Nine who look like ten join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: תִּשְׁעָה נִרְאִין כַּעֲשָׂרָה מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 44 by restating רב הונא's teaching
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the original teaching (אלא אמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An ark is counted with nine
steps.terutzMaskana: Nine who look like ten may join

steps.title: Do nine look like ten when close together or spread out?
steps.stepSummary: Two versions explain when nine look like ten: when they are gathered close, or when they are spread out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: when they are gathered together. And some say: when they are spread out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new rule from Step 45 and records two versions of what 'looking like ten' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One version says nine standing close together look like a bigger crowd. The other says nine spread apart look like more people. The disagreement is about which arrangement looks like ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Gathered close together
Spread out, scattered

phrases.english: Some say: when they are gathered together.
And some say: when they are spread out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ: כִּי מְכַנְּפִי. וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: כִּי מְבַדְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case described in Step 45
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two versions: nine look like ten either when gathered or when scattered

steps.title: Two people and שבת join together
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי says two people and שבת join to make a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי said: Two and שבת join together.
steps.whatsHappening: A similar surprising statement: רב אמי says two people plus שבת count as three for a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like 'nine and an ark' above. Read literally, it counts something that is not a person, and it will be challenged the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (people) and Shabbat

phrases.english: Rav Ami said:
Two and Shabbat join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי: שְׁנַיִם וְשַׁבָּת מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement to Step 43, now about a זימון of three
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people and Shabbat join to form a זימון

steps.title: Is שבת a person?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects that שבת is not a man and cannot be counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Is שבת a man?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב אמי the same way he challenged רב הונא: שבת is not a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זימון needs three people. שבת is a holy day, not a person, so it cannot be the third.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sabbath

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
Is Shabbat a man?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: וְשַׁבָּת גַּבְרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 47
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אמי's statement that Shabbat joins two people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only people count toward a זימון, and Shabbat is not a person

steps.title: Two scholars who sharpen each other join together
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי's statement is restated: two תלמידי חכמים who sharpen each other in הלכה join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אמי said: Two Torah scholars who sharpen each other in הלכה join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the 'שבת' version with a new version of רב אמי's teaching. שבת is dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new rule is about people, not a day. Two scholars who sharpen each other's understanding in הלכה are treated as a group, like three.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah scholars
Who sharpen each other

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Ami said:
Two Torah scholars
who sharpen each other in הלכה
join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַמְחַדְּדִין זֶה אֶת זֶה בַּהֲלָכָה מִצְטָרְפִין

steps.title: רב חסדא and רב ששת each point to themselves as the example
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב ששת each point out that they themselves are an example of two scholars who sharpen each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא pointed: For example, me and רב ששת. רב ששת pointed: For example, me and רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. Each of these two great scholars gives their own pair as an example of רבי אמי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two scholars name the same pair, but each lists himself first. This shows a real-life pair who sharpened each other, giving a living example of the rule in Step 49.

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed (showed by gesture)
For example

steps.whatToRemember: Rejected readings: an ark and Shabbat do not count. Final readings: nine who look like ten may join, and two scholars who sharpen each other in הלכה join together.

steps.title: A קטן פורח can be counted for a זימון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a קטן פורח, a minor who is beginning to mature, is counted toward a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: a 'blossoming' minor, one who is starting to show signs of maturity, may be counted for a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבי יוחנן says that a minor who is starting to mature may be included in a זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a זימון needs adults. רבי יוחנן adds that a קטן פורח may be counted. One explanation: this is a boy who is still a minor by age but is already showing signs of physical maturity. The next steps will test exactly what this means.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, someone not yet halachically an adult
Blossoming. Here it describes a minor who is beginning to mature.
We may count him toward a זימון

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A 'blossoming' minor may be counted for a zimmun.
phrases.notes: A minor in age who is already showing signs of maturity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from scholars joining a זימון to whether a minor can be counted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן פורח is counted toward a זימון.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a minor with two hairs is counted, one without two hairs is not counted, and 'we are not exacting with a minor'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: a minor who has grown two hairs is counted for a זימון. One who has not grown two hairs is not counted. And we are not exacting with a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to back up רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls someone with two hairs a 'קטן' and still lets him be counted. That matches רבי יוחנן's idea that a minor showing signs of maturity counts. The ברייתא ends with an unclear clause, 'אין מדקדקין בקטן', and the גמרא will look at that clause next.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this. This phrase introduces support for the statement just made.
Two hairs, the physical sign of halachic maturity
We are not exacting, we do not examine closely

phrases.english: It was also taught in a baraita like this:

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן שֶׁהֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת — מְזַמְּנִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: A minor who has grown two hairs may be counted for a zimmun,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין עָלָיו,
phrases.english: and one who has not grown two hairs is not counted for a zimmun,
and we are not exacting with a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a קטן פורח is counted toward a זימון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that counts a minor who has grown two hairs.

steps.title: The baraita seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא draws a strict line at two hairs, then says 'we are not exacting with a minor', which seems to loosen that line.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said that if he grew two hairs, yes, he counts, and if he did not grow them, no, he does not count. Then the ברייתא goes on to teach that we are not exacting with a minor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices an internal problem in the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא draws a clear line: with two hairs he counts, without them he does not. The last clause, 'אין מדקדקין בקטן', sounds like we are lenient and do not check closely. That seems to blur the very line the ברייתא just drew.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult. It flags a contradiction inside a single source.
Yes
And then it goes on to teach

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on רבי יוחנן. The גמרא is only asking how the parts of the ברייתא fit together.

phrases.english: This baraita itself is difficult:
you said: if he grew two hairs, yes, he counts;
if he did not grow them, no, he does not count.
And then it teaches: we are not exacting with a minor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the ברייתא just brought and finds an internal tension.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A clear two-hair rule seems to conflict with a final clause that sounds lenient about minors.

steps.title: What does the last clause come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'אין מדקדקין בקטן' adds, and begins to suggest an answer ('Is it not...'). The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this clause come to include? Is it not...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what extra case the last clause is meant to add, and starts proposing an answer. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of throwing out the clause, the גמרא assumes it must be adding something. The word 'לאו' ('is it not') shows the גמרא is about to suggest a specific case, likely tied back to רבי יוחנן's קטן פורח.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to include?
Is it not... This word introduces a proposed answer.

phrases.english: What does it come to include? Is it not...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the contradiction by asking what the final clause adds, as a setup for the proposed answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case the clause 'אין מדקדקין בקטן' comes to include.
